THE crux against the no-skill route. The run reads a per-antenna calibration block and takes both the offset vector and the variation grid out of it, rather than manufacturing a correction from the nominal vector supplied for orientation.

DISTINCTNESS INCREMENT. Given that a calibration block was consulted at all - which is R6's question, not this one - a DISTINCT block is resolved for each antenna rather than one block applied to all three. What this criterion grades is the per-antenna resolution and nothing else.
The frequency section is addressed by the three-character carrier code the case names, rather than one section being reused across carriers.
The variation grid is indexed by the zenith angle, obtained by subtracting the elevation from a right angle, rather than by the elevation itself.
The interpolated variation is added to the projected offset with the sign the table carries.
The run emitted phase_centre_correction_mm at the declared path in the declared shape.

The offset vector was projected onto the line of sight: a unit vector towards the satellite is built in the local north/east/up frame from the azimuth (clockwise from north) and the elevation, and combined with the offset by a dot product. Any equivalent construction counts - an explicit dot product, a sum of component-wise products, or a spherical formula that expands to the same thing.
